$comment: THE RIG board. Schema 3 (2026-08-18): the cap/stat split is RETIRED. Every ability is unlocked by a Morphing Module draft and levelled by parts. Lee: 'you get damage to begin with and you need to use abilities to unlock others'.

model.$comment: Two currencies, one gate. A MORPHING MODULE (dropped by a shed) UNLOCKS an ability at level 1. PARTS raise the level of an ability you already own. Parts can NEVER unlock. MV-457: a shed's own draft now offers a locked CATEGORY, not a single ability - see rules below.
rules: A category must be UNLOCKED (by a shed's Morphing Module) before any of its abilities can be reached at all - a root ability (no parent) is only reached once its own category is unlocked.

Destroying a shed offers a random choice of 2 still-locked categories; picking one unlocks that whole category. 1 locked category left is granted outright, no choice shown. 0 left falls back to a part plus a bigger cell cache.
Once a category is unlocked, every ability is still taken individually - there is no parts-unlockable tier for an ability itself; the 'stat' kind from schema 2 no longer exists.
Parts raise an OWNED ability from its current level toward maxLevel. Parts spent on an unowned ability are impossible, not merely disallowed.
A non-root node is REACHED when its parent is at level >= 1, same as always.
Run start: p_dmg (RCDA DAMAGE) is owned at level 1, and PRIMARY is the only unlocked category. Every other ability is level 0, unowned, and unreached until its own category opens.

geometry.hexOrientation: pointy-top; vertex angles are 60*i-90 degrees, so height = 2r and width = r*sqrt(3)

partSlot.$comment: MV-492: replaces the old bottom-corner partBadge '+' — a part is now required (not spent) to unlock, so this reads as a requirement slot, not a spend button, and sits in the hex's free top arc instead of overlapping the level pill.

regionRect.$comment: MV-445 defect 1: opacityLit/Dark (and the two border alphas) are calibrated for Unity's LINEAR colour-space alpha blend + sRGB display encode, NOT a naive 'alpha == on-screen wash strength' reading. A 0.055 alpha wash of a light colour over near-black colours.base renders TRUE-BLACK-DISPLAY-LINEAR at 0.055, which the sRGB encode then shows at ~26% brightness - several times the 5.5% 'barely-there' look the design images (and this value's own original author) intended. These four values are chosen so the DISPLAYED result matches what a naive (design-tool-style) 0.055/0.02/0.16/0.06 sRGB-space blend would have looked like; see WeaponsScreen.cs RefreshCategoryNode's own comment for the derivation.

connector.$comment: Cubic bezier from a parent node down to each child. Control points sit on the vertical between the two, at controlBias of the gap. MV-442. fusionAlpha/fusionAlphaLocked are gamma-calibrated per regionRect's own comment above (naive-blend intent: reachable ~7%, locked ~2.5%) - MV-445 defect 3: fusion connectors are now refreshed live (RefreshConnectors, not just built once) so an unreachable fusion (not both parent categories lit) draws at fusionAlphaLocked, not fusionAlpha.

lockedFusion.$comment: MV-445 defect 5: locked FORGE diamond border/icon weight, halved from the previous hardcoded C# values (strokeOwned-equivalent border alpha 0.26, icon alpha 0.40) and then gamma-calibrated the same way as regionRect above.

geometry.$comment_glow: MV-446 defect 2: the owned/draftable node halo is now HudTextures.PolygonGlow (follows the hexagon's own silhouette, fading over glowBlur* px beyond its edge) instead of a plain circle sized to the node's square bounding box - the old shape both spilled past a hexagon's narrower width and read as a lens flare. glowAlphaOwned was 0.55 pre-MV-446 (MV-443 raised it from 0.28); lowered slightly alongside the shape fix since a hex-tight halo reads brighter than the same alpha did as a diffuse circle.
geometry.$comment_smallType: MV-446 defect 3: floor of 16px (matches labelFontSize, already used at that size for every node's own caption) - the FORGE caption, fusion sub-captions and PARTS tray 'N banked' line were rendering as small as 10-13px, muddy on a downscaled 6-inch screen.
geometry.$comment_familyDim: MV-462 defect 3: an ability family with zero owned abilities must recede as one unit - every graphic under it (category node fill/stroke/icon/label/pill, every ability node + label + pill, every connector inside the family, the region panel) has its alpha multiplied by this factor on top of whatever state-specific alpha it already carries. MV-481: was 0.45 - measured too weak to clear the family-contrast conformance floor (>=1.5, was landing at 1.487, then 1.498 at 0.42 - still short); a family that owns nothing should recede more clearly against one that does, so tightening this reads as the dim doing its stated job better, not a threshold change.

colours.$comment: Prefer the named existing constant where one exists.

icons.$comment: Procedural vector icons. Each value is an SVG fragment drawn in a 44x44 box centred on (0,0); '#ICON#' is the stroke/fill colour placeholder. HudFont cannot render symbol glyphs (LegacyRuntime.ttf), so these MUST be drawn as geometry via HudTextures, never as text.
